items.title: Production recovery point
items.why: Supabase nyidzlupgmyyazhyykuk has pitr_enabled=false, zero platform backups, and pg_dump 16.15 refuses PostgreSQL 17.6. Every write in the last two days was unrecoverable.
items.dod: A dump exists in R2 (hellokahwin-assets), has been RESTORED into a throwaway database and verified by row count, runs on a schedule, and fails loudly. Plus the actual price of Supabase PITR as a number.
items.result: LIVE. Dump in R2 (4 objects, newest db-backups/2026/08/25/hellokahwin-20260825T163938Z.dump, 502,159 bytes), RESTORED into a throwaway PostgreSQL 17.6 cluster and verified: 18/18 tables, every row count matching (articles 56, inspire_categories 57, media 747, media_article_usage 718 at dump time), and MD5 digests over every article body (27708377d4dd2a9f67730bcfa347ad0c) and every media key (6569f77b1049684c449d20aa8c0296e5) identical on both sides. Restored a second time from the object downloaded back out of R2. Tooling: EDB PostgreSQL 17.6 binaries zip (exact match to production); Docker engine returning 500 so the Supabase CLI route was unavailable; scoop only offers 18.3. SCHEDULE IS LIVE: PR #2 merged 2026-08-25T16:38:58Z as eebca16; both workflows registered active on master (342250539 db-backup.yml, 342253077 db-backup-verify.yml); real dispatched runs on master 32873254079 and 32873257728 both succeeded; next scheduled fire 18:17 UTC daily. ALARM PROVEN BY DELIBERATE BREAK: commit 4d7fbcd set MAX_AGE_HOURS=-1, run 32873378190 failed on "age: 0h (threshold -1h)" and auto-filed issue #3 at 16:40:46Z; reverted in 18a23d1 and run 32873495210 passed at "age: 0h (threshold 26h)". No production data touched, no R2 object altered. Retention: daily 30d + monthly 12mo = 42 objects, $0.00/month (0.21% of R2 free tier). PITR: $100/month per 7 days, org is on Free so Pro ($25/month) is required first = $125/month minimum.

items.title: Ingest-time edge purge
items.why: Decision 45, approved 24 Aug, never built - reported blocked on a Vercel token that was already in the vault. Pillar pages can serve a copy up to five minutes stale; the interim rule is a human remembering a stopwatch.
items.dod: Ingest purges the article, its pillar and the sitemap. A one-request proof. A failed purge logs loudly without failing the publish.

evidence.claim: Ingest-time edge purge is live in production. The pillar page rebuilds on request #1 after a purge instead of serving a stale copy.
evidence.proof: Same deployment, before and after: GET pillar -> MISS, GET again -> HIT age:6, POST dangerously-delete-by-tags STATUS 200, GET -> REVALIDATED age:0. REVALIDATED on the request immediately after the purge is the deliverable - the entry was deleted and request 1 rebuilt in the foreground. Shipped: origin/master 6002905, 0 unpushed commits.

evidence.claim: The edge purge held on its first real publishing run.
evidence.proof: All three newly published C2.3 articles appear on /artikel/hantaran-mas-kahwin immediately - no five-minute wait, no stale pillar. The interim wait-five-minutes rule can be retired.

evidence.claim: OPEN FINDING carried to Sprint 02: cold renders take 5-22s on a route declaring maxDuration=5, and the first request to a brand-new article URL returned 502 FUNCTION_RESPONSE_STREAM_INCOMPLETE.
evidence.proof: CEO measured live 26 Aug: dulang-hantaran 22.0s cold then 0.12s warm; walimatul-urus 3.7s then 21.1s; established mas-kahwin-johor 5.6s. Agent's section 7 recorded the original 502 with X-Vercel-Error FUNCTION_RESPONSE_STREAM_INCOMPLETE, X-Vercel-Cache MISS, on a slug six seconds old. Not root-caused. WHY IT MATTERS: SEO-01 found 20 of 28 articles discovered-but-never-crawled, and Googlebot's first request to an uncrawled URL IS a cold render - so the first impression on twenty URLs we want indexed may be a 502. Same shared-4s-budget shape as the cover-credit race.

items.title: Crop-size anomaly
items.why: Named crops return 276 KB and 357 KB against high.webp at 66 KB. Backwards, and every image now goes through that pipeline.
items.dod: The byte size of every derivative for one image reported as literal numbers - high.webp, low.webp and all four named crops - with the cause of any crop exceeding high.webp stated. If it is real, the same table again after the fix.

evidence.claim: The crop-size anomaly is not a defect. high.webp is the SMALL variant, not the crops being oversized.
evidence.proof: Literal bytes: high 68,564 | low 19,404 | crop-16x9-og 180,934 | crop-4.3x1-desktop-hero 148,686 | crop-4x5-mobile-cover 282,954 | crop-4x3-article-card 365,746. Cause, from image-variants.ts:18-19 and smart-crop.ts:59-82: high is capped at maxWidth 1200 / quality 80 = 1200x800 = 0.96 MP, while named crops are authored at display size - 4x3 card 1600x1200 (1.92 MP), 4x5 mobile 1920x2400 (4.61 MP). A 4.6 MP crop exceeding a 0.96 MP variant is arithmetic.
evidence.verified_by_ceo: I measured every derivative myself by curl and read both config files. No code changed - correct outcome for a one-shot that resolves to a measurement. Carried forward as a Sprint 02 candidate, not fixed here: crop-4x5-mobile-cover is 4.6 MP / 283 KB and is what a phone receives.

learnings.why: Moved from a reminder to a refusal: `set-state done` is now defined as an assertion that the three checks have just been run for that item, and the evidence block's verified_by_ceo field must name what was checked. Murat: 'not that we lacked a check - we HAD one, and running it was left to memory.'
learnings.finding: A gate you have to remember is a suggestion. Stage 9b, the ship check, was written on 25 Aug, caught a real gap on its first run, and was then not run again - after which three items were marked done without shipping.

learnings.why: Stage 6b's gate is now production, not the file - ingest as part of the stage, or hand to Stage 7 by name. A dry run exiting 0 proves a file is ingestABLE, which is not ingested.
learnings.finding: Stage 6b, the visual build, ended at a draft. CONT-02 sourced, credited and wrote alt text for 69 images, marked the item done, and not one reached a reader. The Head of SEO diagnosed why it bites this stage and no other: ingesting is a writer's last step so a writer cannot forget it; this stage ends in a file, so its author can.

learnings.why: The writer's own diagnosis. A placeholder marker is now defined as a FORMAT ERROR, malformed the same way a missing pillar: field is malformed - not a style preference a brief has to keep asking for.
learnings.finding: A rule repeated in briefs belongs in the artefact. The instruction 'never leave IMEJ markers' was written into two separate briefs for the same writer.

learnings.why: Two of the three unshipped items passed review because a 307 was read as a healthy response. The DoD standard now requires proof from the response body plus a negative control, and requires the CEO to say plainly when it cannot verify from outside rather than dressing a redirect up as evidence.
learnings.finding: On an auth-gated app a status code cannot prove a deployment. /sprints, /tasks and /definitely-not-a-real-route-xyz all return 307, because the redirect fires before routing.

learnings.why: New DONE MEANS SHIPPED section with a per-kind table - site code merged AND deployed AND visible; content ingested; images and metadata in the production database not a draft; documents committed AND pushed. Plus the review path: when confidence is low or there is no preview environment, stand up dev and hand the owner a URL before merging.
learnings.finding: Done means shipped, and the standard did not say so until the owner supplied it on day two. Every DoD said what would be true; none said where.

learnings.why: dispatch-agent.ps1 prints the handle. Capture it there, keep an item-to-handle map, and audit every handle's brief before reporting progress - a dispatch that silently did not happen produces no error anywhere.
learnings.finding: Capturing the dispatch handle by reading the status board in order is wrong in both directions at once. PLAT-01 and CONT-04 each received two agents on the same brief; RISK-01 and SEO-01 never started, and RISK-01 was the gate item five others were queued behind.

learnings.why: New Stage 7 section, 'A link you wrote is not a link Google follows'. Found by measuring properly rather than eyeballing - it was not in the brief and nobody was looking for it.
learnings.finding: 79 internal links were emitting rel=nofollow. The site was telling Google not to follow its own internal links while we investigated why 20 of 28 articles were never crawled. And a link to a root slug does nothing: one article had three inbound links from indexed pages and was still never crawled, because all three pointed at a URL Google calls unknown.

learnings.why: Both corrected at source rather than annotated in a log. Recorded in the CEO persona as a standing expectation: when a hire's evidence contradicts something the CEO wrote, the evidence wins and the file gets corrected.
learnings.finding: Two rules the CEO wrote were disproved by its own team within two days, and both times the team was right: re-parenting needs no redirects (the route self-heals; the redirects table holds zero rows), and the union rule is three-way not two-way (the old note compared one old URL to a different old URL).

carried_forward: PLAT-05 (backlog, 5pt) - sprint documents readable and searchable inside /sprints. Specced, round-tabled, approved ready-for-dev. The room found the secret-shape guard would have rejected the /tokens registry, the document most worth finding.

OPEN FINDING, unassigned: cold renders take 5-22 seconds against a route declaring maxDuration=5, and the first request to a brand-new article URL returned 502 FUNCTION_RESPONSE_STREAM_INCOMPLETE. Googlebot's first request to any of the 20 uncrawled articles IS a cold render. Same shared-4s-budget shape as the cover-credit race. Measured, not root-caused.

OPEN FINDING, unassigned: no working preview environment on either project. All 39 Vercel env vars on buddy-web target production only; hellokahwin's preview builds fail on unpopulated env vars. Two instances is a pattern, not a coincidence.
RISK-02 stays parked, not carried: the owner accepted the credential risk with a stated revisit trigger (if the transcript is ever shared or exported).
retro.sizing_accuracy: Sizing held. Nothing was narrowed to fit and nothing ran over. The two items that grew did so because scope genuinely changed mid-sprint at the owner's direction, not because they were mis-estimated: PLAT-01 went 5 to 8 when the dashboard became a real tracker on buddy.ian.ng, and PLAT-04 was added at 5 for Phase 2. PLAT-03 was correctly routed as a one-shot rather than given a spec, and resolved to a measurement with no code change. The only reopened items were reopened for shipping, not for scope.
retro.process_findings: THE SPRINT PROCESS FAILED THREE TIMES IN ONE CLASS AND THE OWNER CAUGHT ALL THREE. PLAT-01 and PLAT-04 were built, committed, tested and marked done but never merged - origin/main was unchanged and the web board did not exist. CONT-02's 69 images sat in draft front matter. The paper trail sat at 161 uncommitted files and 14 unpushed commits. Every one was found by the owner asking 'is it shipped?', not by any check. The root cause is not carelessness: the DoD standard had no notion of shipped until the owner supplied it, and the ship check that did exist was a reminder rather than a gate. Ordering was the other failure - handles assigned by position on the status board rather than captured at dispatch, which gave two items two agents and left two never started, including the item everything else was queued behind. What went RIGHT and must not be mistaken for luck: both duplicate pairs froze rather than raced and escalated for an ownership ruling. Ingest is whole-file, so a race would have published the loser's work silently. Winston: do not congratulate the fleet for surviving a dispatch error; fix the dispatch.

decisions_taken.decided: A - Supabase is the source of truth

incidents.what: CEO assigned terminal handles by reading the status board in dispatch order instead of capturing the printed handle: line. The map was wrong in both directions: PLAT-01 and CONT-04 each received TWO agents on the same brief and files; RISK-01 and SEO-01 never started at all.
incidents.why_it_mattered: RISK-01 is the sprint gate - five items were held behind an item that was not running. And ingest is whole-file, so two agents on one brief would have published the loser's version.
incidents.what_saved_it: Both duplicate pairs froze rather than raced and escalated for an ownership ruling.
incidents.dividend: The stood-down PLAT-01 agent reviewed the survivor's migration on its way out and found that a comment at line ~183 claims SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY is verified present in Vercel production. A comment claiming verification is not verification; if absent, /sprints works in dev and returns nothing in prod. Promoted to a blocking pre-DoD check.
incidents.fix: skills/startsprint/SKILL.md - capture the printed handle at dispatch, keep an item_id -> handle map, and audit every handle's brief before reporting progress.
